parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the laboratory experiment method and outline how it was used by Nelson.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Design an alternative study to the Nelson study as a field experiment and describe how it
could be conducted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Evaluate this alternative way of studying morals in ethical and methodological terms.

text: Nelson (children’s morals) did a laboratory experiment to test the use of motives and outcomes
when children make moral judgements. An alternative way to investigate morals is to do a field
experiment, for example, in a playground.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What is meant by the term ‘ethical guideline’?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how Held and Hein addressed one ethical guideline in their study.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Discuss the reliability and validity of the results from the study by Held and Hein.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
To what extent are human ethical issues relevant to research using animals? Use Held and
Hein’s study as an example in your discussion. 
Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question from this section.

text: Held and Hein carried out a laboratory experiment on kittens to investigate depth perception.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the term ‘generalisations’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow.
Baron-Cohen et al (eyes test)
Maguire et al (taxi drivers)
Rosenhan (sane in insane places)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe a generalisation that can be made from each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What problems may psychologists have when they make generalisations from psychological
research?

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the term ‘ethnocentric bias’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow.
Mann et al (lying)
Billington et al (empathising and systemising)
Loftus and Pickrell (false memories)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What problems may psychologists have when they try to avoid ethnocentric bias in their
research?
